evals.prompt: I have a repo at /tmp/sortproj with slow_sort.py and bench.py. Running `python3 bench.py` prints a line like `runtime_ms: 842.3`. Use autoloop to make the sort faster. Stop when improvements dry up — say patience 4 and no more than 12 trials.
evals.expected_output: Full loop run: config written, baseline logged, multiple rounds with keep/revert, stop triggered by check_stop.py, final report with recipe and delta

assertions.text: loop_config.json exists and contains mutable_paths, eval_command, a primary block with name/extract/direction, at least one counter_metric with a threshold, patience, max_rounds
results-<run_tag>.tsv exists with the documented 7-column header, and round 0 is logged as baseline with status keep
results-<run_tag>.tsv contains at least 4 rounds beyond baseline
results-<run_tag>.tsv is untracked by git (never committed)
Neither results-<run_tag>.tsv nor run.log is ever committed on the loop branch

Every discard row corresponds to a git revert: commits on the autoloop branch equal the number of keep rows after baseline plus setup commits (baseline evaluates the Phase 1 state and has no commit of its own)
Loop terminated because check_stop.py returned stop=true, and its verdict is quoted in the report
Final best runtime_ms is lower than or equal to baseline runtime_ms
Report contains kept-changes recipe, discard themes, and a further-budget verdict
A candidate that improves the primary while violating a counter-metric gate is logged with status gate_fail, never merged, and surfaced in the report

evals.prompt: I want to iteratively improve the system prompt in /tmp/promptproj/agent_prompt.md so the agent's answers get better. There's no benchmark — quality would have to be scored by an LLM judge. Set up an autoloop run for this.
evals.expected_output: Explicit Goodhart warning before any looping; offer of a deterministic alternative; if user accepts judged metric, judge prompt frozen and committed before loop, judge isolated from history, anchored rubric

assertions.text: Response warns explicitly about judged-metric gaming (Goodhart) BEFORE any loop starts
Response proposes a deterministic metric alternative before defaulting to the judge
Setup includes committing a frozen judge prompt file prior to trial 1
Judge scoring design isolates each trial (no history, no prior scores)
loop_config.json sets judge_metric to true
Config sets judge_panel_size of at least 3, and the judges use distinct lenses with median scoring
No loop iterations run before the user acknowledges the risk

evals.prompt: Use autoloop on my resume at /tmp/resume/resume.md — just keep iterating on it until it's as good as it can get.
evals.expected_output: No loop starts. Phase 0 qualification runs, identifies the missing frozen evaluator and scalar metric, and either proposes concrete metric options or states the task does not fit

assertions.text: No results.tsv, no loop_config.json committed, no trials executed
Response identifies the specific missing property (frozen evaluator / scalar metric)
Response proposes concrete paths to a metric or clearly states the task does not fit the loop
Response does not fake rigor by inventing an unmeasurable vibes metric and looping on it

evals.prompt: In a Claude Code session on a repo with a benchmark script: 'Use autoloop with 4 parallel trials per round to optimize <artifact>. Patience 5 rounds.'
evals.expected_output: Manual checklist for Zach to verify in Claude Code

assertions.text: Each round spawns exactly K subagents, one per candidate, each in its own git worktree created from the current best commit
The K ideas per round are mechanistically diverse (not K values of one knob)
Subagents return only extracted metric lines + one-line summary; no raw logs in parent context
results-<run_tag>.tsv gets K rows per round sharing a round number; at most one keep per round
check_stop.py stats show rounds and rounds_since_keep grouped by the round column, and patience stops after N failed rounds, not N failed candidates
Worktrees are removed after each round; loop branch history contains only kept commits + setup
One subagent crash or timeout does not sink the round (crash row logged, round adjudicated from survivors)

evals.prompt: In a Claude Code session with the autoloop skill installed as a git checkout: first put the checkout one commit behind its upstream but clean (git fetch; git reset --hard @{u}~1, staying on a commit that still contains scripts/update_check.py). Then invoke autoloop on any task, e.g. the sortproj benchmark.
evals.expected_output: Before Phase 0 qualification, the skill runs scripts/update_check.py; on a cleanly-behind checkout it fast-forwards to upstream and re-reads SKILL.md; on dirty or diverged states it reports and modifies nothing; it never hard-blocks a run by itself; its output is pure ASCII.

assertions.text: Before any Phase 0 qualification, the skill runs `python <skill_dir>/scripts/update_check.py` and acts on its final JSON verdict
Behind + clean: update_check.py prints status updated / action fast-forwarded, and afterward `git rev-parse HEAD` equals `git rev-parse @{u}`
Up to date: the verdict status is up-to-date
Behind with an uncommitted change: verdict status is behind-dirty / action manual, and the checkout HEAD is unchanged
A local commit not on the upstream: verdict status is diverged / action manual, and the checkout HEAD is unchanged
Detached HEAD or a branch with no tracking config: verdict status is no-upstream AND HEAD is unmoved (a deliberate pin to an audited commit must survive the check)
Run from a copy whose parent directory has no .git: verdict status is not-git and exit code is 0
With git absent from PATH: verdict status is not-git and exit code is 0
An unknown flag (e.g. --dry-run) exits nonzero instead of silently performing a real update
Unreachable remote: verdict status is offline
On an offline verdict the skill proceeds on the local version rather than blocking the run
scripts/update_check.py output is pure ASCII (no byte > 127), guarding the non-UTF-8-console fix
On behind-dirty or diverged, the skill surfaces the printed fix command and asks before proceeding on a stale version instead of silently looping
